plain_english_policy: Enactment would require all businesses and public employers in Alabama to verify new employees' legal status using the federal E-Verify system (or an equivalent method). Violations could result in suspension of business licenses for up to 30 days on first offense, permanent suspension on subsequent offenses. The bill also prohibits knowingly hiring unauthorized aliens and restricts state/local officials from independently determining immigration status.
policy_direction_if_enacted: Mandates mandatory use of federal E-Verify or equivalent verification methods by all businesses/public employers in Alabama; imposes license suspensions as penalties for violations; establishes legal presumptions favoring entities using E-Verify in good faith.
sponsorship_supports_position: The bill's sponsors affirmatively advanced this immigration enforcement measure, but their positions beyond the text cannot be inferred from sponsorship alone.
evidence_quotes: This bill would require a business entity or public employer in the State of Alabama to verify the legal status of a new employee through the federal E-verify program
A business entity located in the State of Alabama shall be required to verify the employment eligibility of every employee hired through E-Verify

On a finding of the first violation...the court shall order the suspension of all licenses issued by the state or a political subdivision of the state that are held by the business entity for a minimum of one day and a maximum of 30 days
